chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari told us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, he said: Muqatil ibn Sulayman told me, he said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The Merciful, who above the Throne is evened.'
He said: He evened Himself with everything, and thus, there is no thing that is closer to Him than another thing.

key_terms.اسْتَوَىٰ: He evened Himself / He established Himself
key_terms.الرَّحْمَٰنُ: The Merciful, one of the names of Allah
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne, a symbol of divine authority and dominion

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah is described as 'evened' above the Throne?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'Istawa' (establishing/rising) not as physical movement but as divine equality and encompassing presence, asserting that no creature is closer to Allah is nearer to than another. This aligns with the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* (divine unity), rejecting anthropomorphic attributes (*Tajsim*) by emphasizing that Allah's relation to creation is one of absolute proximity and equality rather than spatial location. The explanation underscores that 'Throne' (*Arsh*) symbolizes the totality of creation, reinforcing the concept of Allah's omnipresence without being confined to it.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Hasan bin Mahbub, that he said: I was told by Muqatil bin Sulayman, that he said: I asked Ja’far ibn Muhammed, peace be upon them both,
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «The Merciful, who above the Throne is evened.» [20:5]
He said: He evened Himself with everything, and thus, there is no thing that is closer to Him than another thing.
